{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ga-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"a0d14ac57e94dead5634fa89728123ce327a38c3e6e10e97d892269f114421b8","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ga-class-c:lineage:56","source_registry_sha256":"e082bc406bec2cfadcd011c884a136274a0200b40ae5a1536777a259a1b09eb3","source_liveness_sha256":"899bb7b77ecc9a36dd3203950c0cfa2065e4529a11881605f77eacb7d739a757"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Withdrawal of driving privileges and points","heading":"Withdrawal of driving privileges and points","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## Withdrawal of driving privileges and points

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
DDS may withdraw driving privileges when evidence establishes that a driver is habitually dangerous or negligent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Cancellation may follow missing or incorrect application information or later ineligibility. A resident may reapply after meeting the requirements and becoming eligible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Revocation terminates driving privileges for the period established by DDS's formal action; a resident may apply for a new license after that period. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
After revocation, a nonresident may apply to have Georgia driving privileges reinstated rather than seeking return of a Georgia resident's license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Suspension temporarily withdraws driving privileges for a specified period or until the reinstatement conditions are met. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
After the required suspension period, a resident may seek reinstatement of the license or licensing eligibility; a nonresident may seek reinstatement of Georgia driving privileges. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Courts report convictions affecting driving privileges or requiring an entry in the permanent driving record; DDS updates the record when a conviction arrives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
For a person licensed or residing elsewhere, Georgia forwards conviction information to that jurisdiction's licensing authority. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
A qualifying conviction can suspend a nonresident's Georgia driving privilege or an unlicensed person's eligibility to obtain a Georgia license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
Reported convictions from another state or country can be placed on a Georgia driver's record and treated like Georgia convictions for withdrawal purposes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
A nonconviction withdrawal can arise from refusing required chemical testing, failing to appear or respond to a citation, unpaid child support or an unpaid Super Speeder charge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook also lists safety-responsibility action, medical action and an adult's request to revoke a minor's credential among nonconviction withdrawal grounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
A conviction for impaired driving, a vehicle-related felony, fleeing an officer, hit-and-run or racing is among the handbook's mandatory-suspension grounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A01
Driving without insurance, driving with withdrawn registration, or driving while the license is suspended, revoked or canceled are also listed suspension grounds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists vehicular homicide, first-degree vehicular feticide and serious injury by vehicle as offenses causing suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A01
A court may impose suspension for violating a license restriction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A01
For a driver younger than 21 at conviction, the additional listed suspension offenses include reckless or aggressive driving, unlawfully passing a school bus and improper passing on a hill or curve. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A01
The handbook also lists speeding at least 24 miles per hour over the limit or another 4-point offense as suspension grounds for a driver younger than 21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A01
Accumulating at least 4 points during 12 months before age 18 is listed as an additional suspension ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
The implied-consent section describes state chemical testing to determine alcohol or drug impairment and possible license consequences for refusal or a result at the legal limit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
After submitting to the required state tests, the handbook describes an entitlement to additional chemical testing by qualified personnel chosen by the driver, at the driver's expense. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A03
A habitual-violator declaration can cause revocation based on a third conviction within 5 years for a combination of the specified serious offenses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=49]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A03
The habitual-violator list includes impaired driving, vehicular homicide or serious injury, hit-and-run, racing, fleeing, reckless stunt driving, withdrawn-registration operation and a felony using a motor vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=49]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A03
Refusing a notified reexamination supported by reasonable grounds can cause revocation; the handbook also permits action when evidence establishes that a person cannot drive safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=49]

Misconceptions: A withdrawal period ending does not itself establish that every reinstatement requirement has been met; a limited permit does not restore unrestricted driving.
Mnemonic: Reason, action, conditions, application, reinstatement.
Glossary: Cancellation addresses eligibility or application defects; suspension is temporary withdrawal; revocation terminates the privilege for the imposed period.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Testing rights, penalties, points programs, deadlines and permit eligibility retain current legal review and are not individualized legal advice.
